OpenAPI 3.0.0
# Sherlock Interview API
Server:https://app.sherlock.sh/api/public/v1
Client Libraries

- agent_name
Type: string
Custom name for the AI agent joining the meeting
- auth_header
Type: string
max length:
2048
Custom auth header name for callback webhook. Must be provided together with auth_token and auth_url.
- auth_token
Type: string
max length:
2048
Custom auth token value for callback webhook. Must be provided together with auth_header and auth_url.
- auth_url
Type: string
max length:
2048Format: uri
Callback webhook URL (http/https). Must be provided together with auth_header and auth_token.
- candidate_email
Type: stringFormat: email
Candidate email address. If provided without image, a verification email is sent.

Request Example for post/interviews
```curl
curl https://app.sherlock.sh/api/public/v1/interviews \
--request POST \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_SECRET_TOKEN' \
--data '{
"candidate_name": "John Doe",
"interview_link": "https://meet.google.com/abc-defg-hij",
"started_at": "2026-01-25T14:30:00Z",
"candidate_email": "john.doe@example.com",
"agent_name": "Sherlock Integrity",
"image": "/9j/4AAQSkZJRgABAgAAAQABAAD//gAPTGF2YzYyLjYuMTAwAP...",
"auth_header": "Authorization",
"auth_token": "webhook-secret-token",
"auth_url": "https://example.com/hooks/interview-report"
}'
```

title: Authenticate to Sherlock AI with API keys on CloudFerro Cloud
snippet:
# Authenticate to Sherlock AI with API keys on CloudFerro Cloud
Sherlock AI uses API keys to authenticate programmatic requests to AI models. You create API keys inside a Sherlock AI project in the control panel and then use them from your application, automation script, or backend service.
Treat every API key as a secret. Do not share it with other users, commit it to a repository, paste it into documentation, or expose it in client-side code such as browsers and mobile applications. Production requests should go through your own backend, where the key can be loaded from an environment variable or a secrets management service.
## Prerequisites
Before you start, make sure that:
1. You can log in to the Sherlock AI control panel.
2. You have access to the project where the API key will be created.
3. Your account has permissions to manage API keys in that project.
4. You know where the key will be stored after creation, because Sherlock AI shows the generated key only once.
## Step 1: Open API Keys
Log in to the Sherlock AI control panel and open the project in which you want to create the key. In the left navigation menu, select **API Keys**.
The API keys page lists the keys already created in the current project. Use this page to check existing keys, create a new one, and manage project-level authentication for programmatic access.

## Step 2: Start creating a new key
Click **Add API key** to open the key creation window. Enter a clear name for the key, for example the name of the application, service, environment, or automation workflow that will use it.
A descriptive name is important later, especially when several keys exist in the same project. It helps you recognize which application uses which key and makes key rotation safer.

## Step 3: Generate and copy the key
After entering the name, generate the key. Sherlock AI displays the new API key immediately after creation.
Copy the key at this stage and store it in a secure location. This is the only time the full key is shown. If you close the window before saving it, you will need to create another key.

## Step 4: Verify that the key was created
After copying the key, return to the API keys page and verify that the new entry is visible in the list. The list shows the key name and creation date, which helps you identify recently created keys and distinguish them from older credentials.
Keep only the keys that are still needed. When a key is no longer used, replace it in your application first,

# Sherlock API
## Introduction
This API allows the semantic annotation of texts and web URLs. The first step is annotate a text or url and then ask for information from the annotated entities.
Any API call must have the identifier of the application in the request headers
**Sample:**
```
Authorization: Bearer {APP_TOKEN}
```
## Annotation
| API | Description |
|---|---|
| [POST api/Annotation](/v1/en/Help/Api/POST-api-Annotation) | Allows you to annotate a text or an url to obtain entities, topics and the text with augmented reading. |
## GetEntity
| API | Description |
|---|---|
| [GET api/GetEntity?uri={uri}&lang={lang}&big={big}](/v1/en/Help/Api/GET-api-GetEntity_uri_lang_big) | Get the data of a given entity. |

title: Get started with the Sherlock API on CloudFerro Cloud
snippet:
An application needs an API key, a model identifier, and an endpoint before it can request an answer. Sherlock provides an OpenAI-compatible API for language, vision, and embedding models. You can use curl for a first terminal request or the OpenAI Python client for an application running on your computer or a virtual machine.
The procedure below prepares the client, lists available model IDs, and sends a first chat request. The same account and project used in My Portal provide the context for the API key.
## Prerequisites
No. 1 **Access to a Sherlock project**
Complete [account and organization setup through My Portal](https://docs.cloudferro.com/en/latest/sherlock/How-to-set-up-Sherlock-AI-on-CloudFerro-Cloud.html), then [create or select a project](https://docs.cloudferro.com/en/latest/sherlock/Manage-Sherlock-projects-on-CloudFerro-Cloud.html). Creating a project requires administrator privileges in the organization; for an existing project, use the access granted to your account.
No. 2 **An API key for that project**
Follow [Authenticate with API keys](https://docs.cloudferro.com/en/latest/sherlock/Sherlock-authentication-API-keys-on-CloudFerro-Cloud.html) to create and securely store a key. Your account needs permission to manage API keys in the selected project. Have the key available for the environment-variable setup below.
Warning
Keep the API key secret. Do not share it, commit it to a repository, or expose it in browser or mobile application code. Production requests must pass through your backend, where the key is loaded from an environment variable or a secret store.
No. 3 **Tools for the examples you want to run**
For Python, install [Python](https://docs.python.org/3/using/index.html) and [pip](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/installation/). For terminal requests, install [curl](https://curl.se/download.html). The curl commands below use Bash syntax. On Windows, use a Bash environment for those commands or run the Python examples from PowerShell.
## Model types
Choose a model for the kind of result your application needs. A model ID identifies the model in an API request; copy it exactly from the models endpoint rather than assuming a name in an older example is still available.
| Model type | Use |
|---|---|
| Language model | Generate a text answer from a prompt or conversation. |
| Vision-capable model | Answer a question that includes an image as well as text. |
| Embedding model | Convert text into numerical vectors for search and sim

title: Searching your data
snippet:
- You can reach the deployment with one of: `curl`, the Sherlock Python SDK (`sherlock-client`), or the platform CLI ([`pharia`](https://github.com/Aleph-Alpha/pharia-cli)).
## Client setup
Each example below is shown for three clients. All three call the same REST API at `https://sherlock.{ingressDomain}/api/v1`; the SDK and the CLI wrap the requests shown in the **curl** tab. Every request requires a bearer token. The deployment’s IAM sidecar validates the token and adds the caller’s user identity to the request, and Sherlock authorizes the request against that identity.
- curl
- Python SDK
- Platform CLI
Log in once with the platform CLI, then export the deployment URL and a token:
```bash
pharia --env aleph-alpha iam login    # one-time OAuth login via your browser
export SHERLOCK_URL="https://sherlock.{ingressDomain}"
export AA_TOKEN="$(pharia --env aleph-alpha iam token)"
```
Pass `-H "Authorization: Bearer $AA_TOKEN"` on every call. A platform token from any other source also works; the API only reads the header. Requests with a JSON body use `--json` (curl 7.82.0 or later), which sends the body and sets the `Content-Type` and `Accept` headers to `application/json`. To read the body from a file, use `--json @body.json`.
Install the client from the Aleph Alpha package index:
```bash
pip install sherlock-client --extra-index-url https://alephalpha.jfrog.io/artifactory/api/pypi/holmes/simple
```
Then create a client for the deployment and a handle for the store you are searching:
```python
import os
from sherlock import SyncSherlock
client = SyncSherlock(
url="https://sherlock.{ingressDomain}",
token=os.environ["AA_TOKEN"],
)
store = client.v1.search_stores("<store-id>")
```
`url` and `token` default to the `SHERLOCK_BASE_URL` and `SHERLOCK_TOKEN` environment variables, so `SyncSherlock()` without arguments works when those variables are set. `Sherlock` is the async client and has the same API. Use either client as a context manager (`with SyncSherlock(...) as client:`) to close the connection pool when you finish.
The platform CLI ([`pharia`](https://github.com/Aleph-Alpha/pharia-cli)) handles authentication. Log in once; every subsequent command uses the cached token:
```bash
pharia iam login    # one-time OAuth login via your browser
```
